newsitem.title: UK: British drug convict arrives from Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: British drug convict arrives from Bangkok.

text.p: British drugs trafficker Sandra Gregory, jailed for 25 years in Thailand, arrived in Britain on Thursday to serve the remainder of her sentence.
Gregory, 32, was led in handcuffs from the British Airways flight from Bangkok after she arrived at Heathrow airport and taken to Holloway women's prison in north London, officials said.
She was accompanied on the flight by three other British prisoners, also convicted and jailed by Thai courts for drug offences.

Gregory, from Halifax in northern England, was detained with Robert Lock from Cambridge in February 1993, as they were about to board a flight to Japan. Anti-narcotics police found 102 grams (3.6 ounces) of heroin in her possession.
She pleaded guilty but told the court that Lock had paid her to smuggle the heroin out of Thailand.
In February 1996, she was sentenced to 25 years in jail for heroin smuggling. A death sentence was commuted because she confessed and Lock was found not guilty.
The departure of the four convicts to serve out their jail terms in Britain was made possible under a bilateral pact between Thailand and Britain.
Under the pact signed in 1991, Britons who have served a certain amount of time in Thailand can apply to be sent home to serve the remainder of their sentence.
Gregory has served four years and four months of her term. She can expect to spend at least another eight years behind bars in Britain.
Thirty-three British citizens, mostly convicted of drugs offences, are serving jail terms in Thailand.
